newsitem.title: PERU: Peru buys fighter jets from Belarus - military sources.
newsitem.headline: Peru buys fighter jets from Belarus - military sources.

text.p: The Peruvian government has purchased 14 Sukhoi-25 fighter jets from Belarus, in addition to its recent acquisition of 18 MiG-29s, air force sources said on Monday.
The sources told Reuters the planes were bought from the former Soviet state of Belarus for an undisclosed price and were currently being held at an air force base in the southern city of Arequipa.
"The MiGs and the Sukhois complement each other ideally, the former for rapid manoeuvres and repelling attacks, the latter for low-flying," said one of the sources, who asked not to be named.
Official military spokesmen said they could neither confirm nor deny the information.

President Alberto Fujimori recently confirmed the purchase of an undisclosed number of MiG fighters, but refused to give more details. In a television interview on Sunday, he promised to disclose full details of the government's recent arms purchases when the moment was appropriate.

The purchase of the planes has raised concerns abroad, particularly in the United States where the State Department last month expressed its "disappointment" and in neighbouring Ecuador, which fought an undeclared border war with Peru last year.
Ecuador, which earlier this year bought four Israeli K-Fir combat planes, has said the purchase of jets by Peru could lead to an arms race.

The air force sources said that in addition to the 14 Sukhoi-25s, Peru also bought 48 short-range missiles, 96 surface-to-air missiles, 36 anti-radar missiles, about 4,000 rockets, 200 bombs and 50,000 rounds of ammunition to equip the planes.

Opposition sources have alleged that Congress recently approved in secret $350 million for the air force to buy new jets. Both Peru and Ecuador lost aircraft during the 1995 conflict which left scores dead and hundreds injured on both sides.
Local military analysts said Peru could be trying to strengthen its hand ahead of the resumption of peace talks on the disputed frontier with Quito later this month in Brasilia.
